text.title: Python FastAPI — Core Rules
text.summary: Thirteen testable rules every python-fastapi application must obey: app lifecycle, schema boundaries, dependency injection, service contract, and the CI gates that hold them.

rule.statement: Routes validate (Pydantic), call exactly one service function, and return a response model. No ORM queries, no business logic, no manual JSON serialisation in routes.
rule.rationale: Thin routes make services unit-testable without HTTP and keep transport concerns isolated.

rule.statement: Use Pydantic v2 BaseModel for every request body and response. Never accept or return a bare dict.
rule.rationale: Pydantic v2 validates input, generates OpenAPI schema, and gives typed access; dict in/out hides field drift.

rule.statement: Acquire one AsyncSession per asyncio task via Depends. Never share an AsyncSession across asyncio.gather or TaskGroup siblings.
rule.rationale: SQLAlchemy sessions are not safe for concurrent use; sharing causes session state corruption and obscure errors.

rule.statement: Use FastAPI BackgroundTasks only for work that completes in <100ms. Route anything longer to Celery / Arq / Taskiq.
rule.rationale: BackgroundTasks run in the same process and can block the response under load; long work needs durable queuing.

rule.statement: Inject every external dependency (DB session, settings, current user) via Depends. Do not import or instantiate at module top level.
rule.rationale: Depends gives per-request lifecycle, testability via dependency overrides, and clean teardown.

rule.statement: Snapshot openapi.json into the repo and diff it on every PR.
rule.rationale: Schema changes are API breaks; explicit diffs catch accidental renames or type narrowing.

rule.statement: Startup and shutdown run inside one `@asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app)` passed as `FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)`. `@app.on_event("startup")` / `("shutdown")` are forbidden.
rule.rationale: `on_event` has been deprecated since FastAPI 0.93 and emits a DeprecationWarning at boot. `lifespan` owns both phases in one scope, so a resource opened before `yield` is still released when startup raises after it.

rule.statement: Each entity declares four Pydantic models: `Base` (shared fields), `Create` (input), `Update` (all fields optional), `Response` (output, `model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)`). One model serving several roles is forbidden.
rule.rationale: A single model cannot say "Create requires password", "Response must never contain it" and "Update makes everything optional" at once. Reusing one lets a client set `id` on create and leaks write-only fields into the documented response schema.

rule.statement: Dependencies are declared once as `Annotated` aliases — `DBSession = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_db)]`, `CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]` — and used by name in route signatures.
rule.rationale: Spelling `Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_db)]` on every route makes the signature unreadable and means a change to the provider is a repo-wide edit. The alias makes it one line, and keeps `Depends` out of the route author's way.

rule.statement: Service functions are `async def`, take typed parameters (an `AsyncSession` plus domain values), and return ORM model instances or `None`. Returning a dict or a raw SQLAlchemy `Result` is forbidden.
rule.rationale: The router serialises through `response_model`; handing it a model keeps that the single serialisation point and lets tests assert on attributes. A dict bypasses both the type checker and the OpenAPI contract, so field drift ships silently.

rule.statement: To read a generated id or a server default after an insert, use `await db.flush()` then `await db.refresh(obj)`. Services do not commit; the commit happens once in `get_db` when the request succeeds, with rollback on exception.
rule.rationale: `flush` sends the INSERT and makes server-generated values readable while the transaction stays open, so two service calls in one request remain atomic. A service that commits mid-request destroys that atomicity and leaves the caller unable to roll back.

rule.statement: No synchronous I/O inside an `async def` route or service: no `requests.get`, no sync `Session.query`, no blocking file or subprocess call. Use `httpx.AsyncClient` and `AsyncSession` with `await db.execute(select(...))`; if a blocking call is unavoidable, wrap it in `run_in_threadpool`.
rule.rationale: A blocking call inside a coroutine stops the whole event loop, so every other in-flight request waits for it. The symptom is latency that collapses only under concurrency — which is exactly the load level the async stack was chosen for.

rule.statement: Interactive docs are gated by environment: `docs_url="/docs" if settings.debug else None` (same for `redoc_url` and `openapi_url`). Settings come from `pydantic-settings` `BaseSettings` behind an `lru_cache`, never from module-level `os.environ` reads.
rule.rationale: `/docs` publishes every endpoint, parameter and schema in the service — a complete map for anyone probing it. Loading settings through cached `BaseSettings` is what makes the flag testable and keeps a missing variable a startup error rather than a runtime `KeyError`.
